title: What are the shapes in these two grids?
description: Two grids of shapes are solved by adding the two rows that have both kinds of shape, finding one shape with one more step, and filling the empty squares. The second grid also gives column sums and a corner.
teaching_notes: One idea: when no row has only one kind of shape, add two rows so that the numbers of both shapes become equal. Watch for students who guess a value for a shape without testing it in the other row.

source: Fun with Grids: fill the algebra grids
video_script.why: The child finds the shapes of two grids by adding the rows, as the solved grid example found one shape first and carried it on, and then fills the empty squares.
video_script.substitution: Add the two rows to get equal numbers of both shapes, share the total, then find each shape from a row.
video_script.anchor: two grids of shapes: squares and circles in the first, circles and diamonds in the second, with empty squares to fill
video_script.payoff_line: Grid one has square eleven and circle five, and grid two has circle four and diamond seven.

final_answer.value: Grid 1: square 11, circle 5, last row 21. Grid 2: circle 4, diamond 7, third row 15, column sums 18, 15, 15 and 48 in the corner
final_answer.spoken: grid one has square eleven and circle five, and grid two has circle four and diamond seven

maths_rules: Grid 1: 2 squares + circle = 27 and 2 circles + square = 21; adding gives 3 squares + 3 circles = 48, so square + circle = 16.
Square = 27 - 16 = 11 and circle = 16 - 11 = 5; check 22 + 5 = 27 and 10 + 11 = 21; last row circle, square, circle = 5 + 11 + 5 = 21.
Grid 2: circle + 2 diamonds = 18 and 2 circles + diamond = 15; adding gives 3 circles + 3 diamonds = 33, so circle + diamond = 11.
Diamond = 18 - 11 = 7 and circle = 11 - 7 = 4; third row diamond, circle, circle = 7 + 4 + 4 = 15.
video_script.design: One idea: add the two rows so both shapes come equally. The two grids stay in the anchor band and the working sits on the working board.
open_questions: The book prints the grids as figures that the text extract garbles; the rows and the empty squares are placed as the worklist gives them.

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Given, in the first grid, two squares and a circle make twenty seven. Two circles and a square make twenty one.
<bookmark mark='two'/>In the second grid, a circle and two diamonds make eighteen. Two circles and a diamond make fifteen.

marks.find: the things to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find each shape and fill the empty squares.

beats.on_screen: Grid 1, add the rows: 3 squares + 3 circles = 27 + 21 = 48; 1 square + 1 circle = 48 / 3 = 16
narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step one, in the first grid, add the two rows. Three squares and three circles make forty eight.
<bookmark mark='share'/>Share forty eight into three equal parts. A square with a circle makes sixteen.

marks.square: the first row is split into a square and a square with a circle, and 1 square = 27 - 16 = 11 is written
marks.last: 11 + 11 + 5 = 27 and 5 + 5 + 11 = 21 are ticked, and the last row 5 + 11 + 5 = 21 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='square'/>Step two, the first row is one square, plus a square with a circle. That square is twenty seven take away sixteen, which is eleven.
<bookmark mark='circle'/>The circle is sixteen take away eleven, which is five.
<bookmark mark='last'/>Both rows check. The last row has a circle, a square and a circle. Five plus eleven plus five is twenty one.

beats.on_screen: Grid 2, add the rows: 3 circles + 3 diamonds = 18 + 15 = 33; 1 circle + 1 diamond = 33 / 3 = 11
narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step three, do the same in the second grid. Three circles and three diamonds make thirty three.
<bookmark mark='share'/>Share thirty three into three equal parts. A circle with a diamond makes eleven.

marks.diamond: the first row is split into a circle with a diamond, and a diamond; 1 diamond = 18 - 11 = 7 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='diamond'/>Step four, the first row is a circle with a diamond, plus one more diamond. That diamond is eighteen take away eleven, which is seven.
<bookmark mark='circle'/>The circle is eleven take away seven, which is four.
<bookmark mark='third'/>The third row has a diamond and two circles, so seven plus four plus four is fifteen.

marks.first: 4 + 7 + 7 = 18 is written under the first column
marks.others: 7 + 4 + 4 = 15 is written under the second and third columns

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step five, the last row holds the column sums. The first column is four plus seven plus seven, which is eighteen.
<bookmark mark='others'/>The second and third columns are each seven plus four plus four, which is fifteen.
<bookmark mark='corner'/>The corner adds the three sums. Eighteen plus fifteen plus fifteen is forty eight.
